source_a_facts.task: text -> text (causal language modelling / autoregressive generation)
source_a_facts.positional_encoding_note: NemotronHAttention in this checkpoint applies NO rotary embedding in its forward (verified against _captured/nemotron_h_attention golden by the graduated stub). The model is therefore position-id independent; only causality matters.

task_heads.name: text_generation
task_heads.input: 32 distinct natural-language prompts -> AutoTokenizer -> left-padded input_ids [32, T0] (+ attention_mask of ones, so HF and TT see byte-identical inputs)
task_heads.output: 32 independently generated continuations (token ids -> tokenizer.batch_decode -> text)
task_heads.reference: _hf_reference_text_generation(): the SAME 32 padded prompts through model.generate(..., do_sample=False, num_beams=1, max_new_tokens=N, return_dict_in_generate=True, output_scores=True)
task_heads.pass_definition: Gate1 AND Gate2 AND Gate3 all hold in one on-device run of tt/pipeline.py::run_text_generation
task_heads.validation_metric: PCC of the TT per-step next-token logits vs HF gen.scores, computed over ALL 32 batch rows x all N steps (flattened); ALSO per-step PCC and per-sample PCC reported. Gate = min over the 32 samples of that sample's own PCC vs its OWN golden row.
task_heads.behavioral_proof: greedy token-id agreement rate between the TT sequence and gen.sequences over the first N new tokens, per sample; plus the decoded text of both sides printed side by side in the demo.

note_single_call: SOURCE A registers exactly ONE task head for this checkpoint (NemotronHForCausalLM). There is no second Call. Per the orchestration rule ('if two calls share a graduated module, use only ONE agent'), all ten graduated modules belong to Call 1, so Call 1 is built by a single agent against a single shared pipeline.

graduated_modules.verification_method: A module is GRADUATED iff _stubs/<name>.py has a sibling <name>.py.last_good_native OR <name>.py.last_good_sharded snapshot. Enumerated by `ls _stubs/*.last_good_native _stubs/*.last_good_sharded`. Cross-checked against RUN_REPORT.md 'ON_DEVICE (10)' -- the two lists are identical, so none is missed and none is invented.

explicitly_NOT_graduated.why: superseded by nemotron_h_mo_e.py; no .last_good_* snapshot of its own

routing_where_each_graduated_stub_goes.principle: The pipeline drives the NemotronH layer loop itself. Each of the 52 (capped: 7) layers is dispatched by config.layers_block_type. Where two graduated stubs cover overlapping math (a whole-block stub AND its constituent sub-stubs), DIFFERENT layers use DIFFERENT variants, so every stub sits on a real, load-bearing edge of the forward pass and its output feeds the next layer. No coverage sweep, no stub called just to tick a counter.

layer_variants.wiring: x -> nemotron_h_block(x) -> x   (the stub owns pre-norm + Mamba2 SSD mixer + inline gated norm + out_proj all_reduce + residual add)

h = nemotron_h_r_m_s_norm(x); y = nemotron_h_mamba2_mixer(h)  where the mixer's step-12 gated grouped RMSNorm is supplied by the zamba2_r_m_s_norm_gated stub via the mixer's `gated_norm` hook (y_pre_norm, gate) -> normed; x = x + y
h = nemotron_h_r_m_s_norm(x); x = x + nemotron_h_attention(h)   (stub applies its own causal mask, matching sdpa is_causal)
h = nemotron_h_r_m_s_norm(x); x = x + nemotron_h_mo_e(h)   (stub owns router + 128-expert EP mixture + all_reduce + shared expert)

layer_variants.variant: MOE_B / decomposed, shared expert via the MLP stub
layer_variants.wiring: h = nemotron_h_r_m_s_norm(x); logits = nemotron_h_topk_router(h); (idx,w) = on-device route(logits) [sigmoid + e_score_correction_bias + fp32 all-pairs-rank top-6 + norm + routed_scaling_factor]; routed = nemotron_h_experts(h_flat, routing_dense=W); shared = nemotron_h_m_l_p(h); x = x + routed + shared

layer_variants.variant: MOE_C / decomposed, shared expert built from the relu2 stub
layer_variants.wiring: h = nemotron_h_r_m_s_norm(x); logits = nemotron_h_topk_router(h); routed = nemotron_h_experts(h_flat, routing_dense=W); u = ttnn.matmul(h, W_shared_up); a = re_l_u_squared_activation(u); shared = ttnn.matmul(a, W_shared_down); x = x + routed + shared

outside_the_layer_loop.embedding: pipeline-owned ttnn.embedding over the HF embed_tokens weight (on device, no host lookup)
outside_the_layer_loop.final_norm: nemotron_h_r_m_s_norm stub built from model.model.norm_f / model.model.norm
outside_the_layer_loop.lm_head: pipeline-owned ttnn.matmul against the untied lm_head weight (replicated)
outside_the_layer_loop.sampling: ttnn.argmax on device over the last position's logits

sanctioned_stub_extensions.change: accept an OPTIONAL `routing_dense` ttnn tensor (tokens x n_experts) in place of the host-built torch scatter_add_ routing matrix
sanctioned_stub_extensions.why: the graduated body builds its dense routing matrix on the HOST from torch top_k_index/top_k_weights. In a real chained pipeline the routing comes from the on-device router, and a host round-trip would (a) break the fully-on-device host_op_selftest of Command 3 and (b) inject host compute into the hot path. The change is purely ADDITIVE: the existing torch path is untouched, the ttnn expert loop, the ShardTensor2dMesh expert-parallel split and the all_reduce are unchanged. Gate 1 is preserved (still native ttnn, still sharded).

sanctioned_stub_extensions.change: accept an OPTIONAL tp_shard flag that uploads its per-feature `weight` with ShardTensor2dMesh(dims=(None,-1)) instead of ReplicateTensorToMesh
sanctioned_stub_extensions.why: to sit inside the head-sharded nemotron_h_mamba2_mixer its weight must be split on the same TP axis as the mixer's local intermediate width (4096 -> 2048 at TP=2). group_size (512) divides the local width evenly, so the grouped RMS is unchanged. Additive: default stays replicated, which is what its own PCC test uses.

parallelism.tp_axis: cluster_axis = 1 (the last / cols axis) -- every sharded stub already computes _tp_axis = len(mesh_shape)-1 = 1 and all_reduces on it. They agree.
parallelism.shard_enable: the graduated stubs gate their sharded path on env TT_HW_PLANNER_SHARD_RUN; the pipeline sets it before building so the .last_good_sharded bodies take their sharded branch.

scheme_evaluation.scheme: TP column/row-parallel MHA (q/k_exp/v_exp column-parallel, o_proj row-parallel + all_reduce on axis 1)
scheme_evaluation.verdict: COMPATIBLE. Note kernel_findings.json flags TP=4/8/32 as blockers for exactly this reason (n_kv_heads=2); TP=2 is the largest viable degree, which is what the tool selected.

scheme_evaluation.scheme: head-parallel SSD (in_proj column-parallel with a permuted [gate|x|B|C|dt] column order, out_proj row-parallel + all_reduce on axis 1)
same head-parallel SSD as the mixer (it embeds one)
EXPERT-parallel (disjoint expert subsets per chip; replicated router; per-chip one-hot selector; all_reduce of the partial mixture on axis 1; shared expert replicated and added AFTER the reduce)
EXPERT-parallel, same expert axis and same ShardTensor2dMesh(dims=(None,0)) split as nemotron_h_mo_e
TP column/row-parallel un-gated MLP (up_proj column-parallel, down_proj row-parallel + all_reduce on axis 1)
REPLICATED by design (tiny 2688x128 weight, full-width logits feed every chip's expert selection; no collective needed)
scheme_evaluation.verdict: COMPATIBLE -- replication here is the stub's documented TP scheme, not a fallback

scheme_evaluation.scheme: REPLICATED (normalizes the full 2688 hidden dim, which is never split)
elementwise, layout-agnostic; runs on whatever shard it is handed
grouped RMS over group_size=512; replicated by default, TP-sharded on the last dim when injected into the head-sharded mamba mixer

parallelism.sharded_pipeline_proof: The composed pipeline necessarily contains ShardTensor2dMesh uploads (mamba in/out_proj, attention qkvo, MoE/experts expert axis, MLP up/down) AND ttnn.all_reduce(cluster_axis=1) collectives (mamba, attention, MoE, experts, MLP). It is NOT a pure-replication pipeline.
parallelism.dp_axis: rows (axis 0). Weights are replicated across the 2 DP rows by every stub's ShardTensor2dMesh(dims=(None, d)) / ReplicateTensorToMesh. The gate reads back row 0; DP is a throughput axis and must not change the numerics.

batch.how: 32 DISTINCT prompts tokenized together, left-padded to a common T0, threaded as a leading batch dim through embedding -> every layer -> final norm -> lm_head -> argmax. ONE program per step for all 32 rows; no python loop over samples.

stub_batch_audit.status: B is read from hidden_states.shape[0]; _get_consts builds (1,H,T,T) constants that broadcast over B -- verify broadcast actually holds at B=32, else expand to B.
B read from shape[0]; causal mask is (1,1,T,T) -> broadcasts.
B,T read from shape; slices use [B,T,e+1] -- batch-safe.
2-D (tokens, hidden) contract -- the pipeline flattens [B,T,H] -> [B*T,H] and reshapes back. Batch-safe by construction.
HARDCODES a leading 1 in every ttnn.slice bound and in _to_heads/_from_heads reshapes. MUST be taken from x.shape[0] and re-verified -- a hardcoded 1 silently drops samples 2..32.
shape-generic elementwise/matmul; zamba2 reads B,L,C from the tensor. Batch-safe.

batch.pcc_requirement: all 32 rows compared each to its OWN golden row; the gate is the MINIMUM per-sample PCC. 32 identical outputs is a FAIL by construction (the 32 prompts differ).

depth_cap.reason: HARDWARE CEILING, measured not assumed. The checkpoint is 31.58e9 parameters (65.8 GB bf16). Expert weights alone are 128 experts x 2 x 2688 x 1856 = 1.28e9 params per MoE layer x 23 MoE layers = 29.4e9 params = 58.8 GB bf16; expert-parallel at TP=2 halves that to 29.4 GB PER CHIP against ~12 GB of Wormhole DRAM per chip. A full 52-layer resident build cannot fit on 4 chips at any TP degree this model permits (TP>2 is blocked by num_key_value_heads=2 -- see kernel_findings.json).
depth_cap.why_7: layers_block_type[:7] == [mamba, moe, mamba, moe, mamba, attention, moe] -- the shortest prefix that contains all three block types AND enough of each to host all seven layer variants above, hence all 10 graduated stubs. Estimated resident footprint ~5.5 GB/chip (3 MoE x ~1.3 GB EP-halved + mamba/attn ~0.35 GB + embedding 0.7 GB + lm_head 0.7 GB).
depth_cap.golden_is_capped_identically: The HF reference is the SAME checkpoint with model.model.layers truncated to the same 7 blocks (config.num_hidden_layers and layers_block_type truncated to match), embedding / final norm / lm_head intact. TT and HF therefore compute the SAME function; PCC parity is exact-in-scope, not approximated. The generated TEXT from a 7-layer truncation is not meaningful English -- that is a property of the truncation, not of the port, and is stated in the README.
depth_cap.layers_knob: build_pipeline(device, model=None, layers=None, prefill_layers=None, decode_layers=None, ...). layers=None means EVERY layer (all 52) -- honoured, and will exceed DRAM on this box by design. The gate and the demo pass layers=7.

decode_horizon.rule: STOP-TOKEN (priority 1). Stop ids read from generation_config.eos_token_id == [2, 11] (config.eos_token_id == 2 is a subset). Decode halts when EVERY one of the 32 rows has emitted a stop id, or at the safety cap.
decode_horizon.safety_cap: N = min(TT_E2E_MAX_NEW_TOKENS (default 16), config.max_position_embeddings - T0). The default of 16 is a HARDWARE-forced bound, not a magic number: the graduated stubs are stateless full-sequence bodies (no KV / SSM cache), so step k recomputes the whole prefix -- decode is O(N^2) in tokens. Measured on this mesh: 64 local experts over 1024 tokens = 0.30 s, so a 3-MoE-layer forward at B=32 costs ~1 s and 16 steps is ~1 min per side.
decode_horizon.applied_to_both_sides: The SAME N and the SAME stop-id set are passed to model.generate(max_new_tokens=N, eos_token_id=[2,11], do_sample=False) and to the TT loop, so the two sequences always have the same length -- no false mismatch, and the golden is never forced to a count the TT side invented.

gate1_native_ttnn.what: every routed graduated stub is still real ttnn, and every sharded (.last_good_sharded) body keeps its ShardTensor2dMesh + all_reduce
gate1_native_ttnn.how_proved: (a) the pipeline imports the LIVE _stubs/<name>.py and asserts each file is byte-identical to its .last_good_sharded (or .last_good_native where that is the only snapshot) apart from the two sanctioned additive extensions listed above; (b) a static scan of the routed stub sources asserts NO torch compute op (torch.matmul/softmax/layer_norm/F.*/sdpa/argmax/topk...) and no HF submodule call appears in any __call__/_apply_* body; (c) a runtime assert that at least one ShardTensor2dMesh upload and at least one ttnn.all_reduce executed.

gate2_all_invoked.what: all 10 graduated modules actually execute inside the real forward path
gate2_all_invoked.how_proved: tt/_invocation.py registry. Each graduated stub's __call__ calls _invocation.record('<name>') on entry (the pipeline wraps each built stub in a thin recording proxy so the stub sources need not be edited). The e2e test calls _invocation.reset(), runs run_text_generation(), then asserts snapshot() >= set(GRADUATED_MODULES) and prints the set. NO coverage_step / sweep function exists anywhere in the package -- every recorded invocation happened because a real layer needed its output.

gate3_pcc.what: final-output PCC vs the HF golden >= 0.95
gate3_pcc.primary_metric: min over the 32 samples of PCC(TT per-step next-token logits[sample], HF gen.scores[sample]) across all N steps
gate3_pcc.secondary: per-step PCC (all 32 rows) and greedy token-id agreement rate vs gen.sequences
gate3_pcc.print_contract: print(f"e2e PCC={achieved_pcc}") on its own line IMMEDIATELY BEFORE the final assert, on pass AND fail.

forbidden_and_absent: model.generate / hf_model.<submodule>(...) anywhere in run_text_generation or anything it calls
torch compute wrappers (matmul/softmax/layer_norm/embedding/conv/sdpa/relu/gelu/silu/argmax/topk/multinomial/F.*) in the hot path
allowed_hf_use: HF calls inside <stage>_trace_setup() to seed persistent buffers before capture
no_shortcut_contract.joint_rule: every stage is fed the previous TT stage's real ttnn output. No reference tensor is ever injected at a joint.

trace_contract_command3.derivation: config.architectures == ['NemotronHForCausalLM'] and is_encoder_decoder == False -> [prefill, decode]. No speech/vocoder stage.

per_stage.prefill_trace_setup(inputs): pin the sequence axis to a fixed capacity C (default 64, bound = max_position_embeddings); pre-upload the padded input_ids, the causal mask and the mamba shift/tril/neg constants at length C into persistent device buffers OUTSIDE the trace; mask padded positions so [0:T0] is unchanged.
per_stage.prefill_trace_step(): one host-op-free forward at [B=32, C] reading only those buffers.
per_stage.prefill_trace_inputs(): ZERO-ARG; assembles the same tokenized batch the e2e test/demo uses from _captured/_e2e_golden/input_ids.pt (created by tests/e2e/make_golden.py).
per_stage.prefill_trace_items(): returns B * C  (the repeated blocks process every one of the 32 x C prefill positions).
per_stage.decode_trace_setup(inputs): seed the resident per-stream state at capacity C from the prefill result.
per_stage.decode_trace_step(): one token for all 32 rows at the pinned capacity.
per_stage.decode_trace_items(): returns B (32) -- one token retired per row per step.

trace_contract_command3.factory: build_pipeline(device, model=None, layers=None, prefill_layers=None, decode_layers=None, **kwargs) -> the resident pipeline OBJECT (never runs it). Accepts and ignores demo kwargs (prompt/text/...).
trace_contract_command3.stack_discoverability: the object holds self.layers as a plain python list of same-typed NemotronHLayer wrappers (one common base class, one element per built block) plus self.hf (the HF reference) for ground-truth section structure.
trace_contract_command3.trace_capture_selftest(device): per stage: begin_trace_capture -> one step -> end_trace_capture -> execute_trace -> PCC vs the eager reference -> RELEASE before the next stage. trace_region_size sized from the largest stage; on overflow shrink C and PRINT the fallback.
trace_contract_command3.host_op_selftest(): runs the encoded-inputs->logits forward (incl. the ttnn embedding) under scripts.tt_hw_planner.host_op_observer.observe_host_ops(); tokenization and the one-time weight build happen OUTSIDE the observed region. Returns host_op_observer.verdict(ops). This is why nemotron_h_experts needs the device-side routing_dense path.

self_validation_plan: S1  enumerate graduated stubs from the .last_good_* snapshots and assert the set equals RUN_REPORT.md's ON_DEVICE list (10). FAIL LOUD on any drift.
S2  assert every graduated stub appears in the pipeline's layer-variant routing table, and that the table's union == the graduated set (no stub unrouted, no phantom name).
S3  static no-shortcut scan of tt/pipeline.py + every routed stub: no generate(), no hf_model.<submodule>() call, no forbidden torch compute op, no coverage sweep function.
S4  build at layers=7 on the 2x2 mesh with TT_HW_PLANNER_SHARD_RUN set; assert >=1 ShardTensor2dMesh upload and >=1 ttnn.all_reduce executed (sharded pipeline proof).

S5  per-layer sanity before the full chain: PCC each of the 7 built layers' TT output against the corresponding truncated-HF layer output, fed the SAME input. Catches wiring bugs at the joint that a green end-to-end PCC could mask.
S6  run the chained prefill at B=32 and PCC the final logits vs truncated-HF logits for the SAME padded ids. Assert the 32 rows are NOT all identical.
S7  run the N-step decode; compare to model.generate(max_new_tokens=N, do_sample=False) on the truncated model; print e2e PCC then assert >= 0.95.
S8  Gate 2: assert _invocation.snapshot() >= the 10 graduated names; print the set and any missing name.
S9  batch audit: re-run S6 with B=1 vs B=32 and assert row 0 of the B=32 result matches the B=1 result (proves no sample is silently dropped by a hardcoded leading 1).
S10 demo/test share-one-pipeline check: assert demo_text_generation imports run_text_generation from tt.pipeline and defines no second wiring (grep for a duplicated layer loop).
S11 Command 3: trace_capture_selftest(device) True for both stages; host_op_selftest() verdict clean.
S12 re-test every recorded ceiling (the depth cap and any per-stage batch ceiling) at the END, after all fixes, and keep it only if it still reproduces.
